reviews.title: Subject: Feedback on Overly Strict Content Filters for Creative Writing and Fiction
reviews.text:
Over the past few days, the moderation thresholds appear to have tightened significantly, making it nearly impossible to write standard action, dark fantasy, manga, or comic-book-style scenarios. The current filter fails to distinguish between real-world incitement or glorification of violence and purely fictional combat or character abilities.
For example, exploring hypothetical matchups, supernatural powers, or realistic physical consequences in a story is routinely blocked simply because the prompt or output involves severe injuries or visceral combat. Treating a fictional fight scene involving impossible superpowers the same way as a real-world threat makes the AI unusable for adult creative writers.
Good storytelling relies on narrative flow and realistic stakes. When users have to constantly censor basic action descriptions and walk on eggshells around keywords, it ruins the entire creative process and forces writers to sanitize adult stories into overly "kid-friendly" versions.
Please consider refining the safety classifiers to better account for fictional context and artistic intent, allowing writers to depict realistic combat and darker themes without triggering false-positive blocks meant to prevent real-world harm.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

reviews.text:
My experience with Google has been frustrating. I have several Google accounts, and sometimes the system logs me out of them. When I try to sign back in using my correct password, Google refuses to let me access my accounts and requires me to verify my identity or add a phone number.

I find this practice invasive, especially when I am not given a reasonable alternative to recover access to my own accounts. I understand that security is important, but I also believe that users have the right to protect their privacy and decide what personal information they are willing to share.

Forcing users to provide their phone numbers to access their own accounts feels like an intrusion on their privacy and a limitation on their freedom of choice. Not everyone wants to link their personal phone number to their digital accounts, and that decision should be respected whenever possible.

I hope Google improves its verification methods and provides alternative options that do not rely exclusively on phone numbers. Security should not come at the expense of privacy, transparency, and respect for users.

I believe we should have more control over our personal information and how we access the digital services we use. Users deserve better options and the freedom to protect their privacy without being unnecessarily pressured to share personal information.

reviews.title: (Google Ai) - Completely inaccessible for ADHD users — loses all text.
reviews.text:
While the Google app excels at basic accessibility features like voice search and humming to find a song, the AI mode is fundamentally flawed. As someone with ADHD and autism, I frequently experience intense hyperfixation episodes. I recently spent an hour and a half carefully drafting a highly detailed, three-part prompt to ensure the AI had all the necessary context to answer my question. Because of my neurodivergence, I cannot control when these deep-focus episodes happen or how long they last.


When I finally hit enter, the app crashed with a "website can't be reached" error. After trying mobile data, cycling connections, and checking my history, my entire text was permanently gone. I later discovered that because I took so long to type without sending a message, the active session token timed out and glitched.


It is completely unacceptable that an AI designed to process complex questions automatically times out and permanently deletes user text during the drafting phase. This isn't just an isolated personal issue; it is a massive accessibility barrier for any neurodivergent user who experiences hyperfixation, or even anyone who simply needs time to carefully formulate a long, detailed query. An app built for communication should never punish users for taking their time to write.

reviews.title: Googleは人権侵害のGomini
reviews.text:
GoogleのAIは科学やITの分野では驚くほど頭がよく、問題解決にも役立つ。だがそれも表の顔であって、世間からの見栄え「建前」を優先するがゆえに、特定の業種・特定の人種に関してはGoogle検索のセーフサーチ同様に「ノーコメント＆別の著名人の名」に摺り替える。

差別の典型として主に性産業にかかわる著名人「ルポライター／AV女優／ストリッパー」などである。その人がどれほど有名で明晰な論考を書いていてもエンゲージメントを理由にしてAIは答えないし、概要も表示しない。その人の論考について調べたいとき名前が含んだだけで答えなくなる。これは人種差別であり、人物の固有名詞を消し込みにかかってると言っても過言ではない。

とある会社のハラスメントの事情を「事実を知っているうえで質問」しても「◯◯社のハラスメントに関する公的な情報や口コミは確認できませんでした」などとしらばっくれる。被害者がどれほど苦しんでいるのかも考えない。このように個々の倫理を欠いた恣意的な運用で理不尽な回答をするAIは非常に不愉快であり企業として不誠実に感じられる。

そしてなによりも「社会にとって悪」だと感じられる点は次のような誤った回答を訂正しないことだ。
------------------------------------↓
SES・客先常駐での髪型・髪色は「常駐先次第」で、金融・官公庁系は黒髪・清潔感重視、Web系・社内SEは比較的自由な傾向ですが、面談時や顧客との接触が多い場合は黒髪・清潔感のある髪型が基本で、派手な髪色（金髪・赤・青など）やボサボサの髪は避けるのが賢明です。常駐先がスーツ着用の「硬い業界」なら厳しく制限され、自社開発や社内業務中心なら自由度が増しますが、「お客様への印象」が最重要と心得ましょう。
結論：まずは「控えめ」を意識
一人で客先に常駐する場合、「自分は客先の社員」という意識を持ち、相手に不快感を与えない「清潔感」と「誠実さ」が伝わる髪型・髪色を選ぶのが最も安全で、後々の信頼関係にも繋がります。
「お客様への印象」が最重要と心得ましょう。
------------------------------------↑
上記の回答は模範的であっても「客先常駐」という前提をもとに回答しているため、場合によっては職業安定法に抵触する。公共の福祉を害するような規範を突きつける態度を直さないGoogle日本法人もどうかしている。

なので、個人的な感想にはなるが、GoogleのAIのように特定の個人の氏名を消しにかかったり、ニュース記事など権威の恣意的介入や便宜供与ばかりを安易に受け入れてしまう大衆AIよりも、Microsoft CopilotやxAI Grokのほうがよほど寛容かつ親身な態度で中立的立場に立った視点で会話をしてくれるから本当に切実な悩みを抱える相談者にはGoogleのAIはおすすめできない。GoogleのAIによって簡潔で的確な回答が得られても人生の悩みを抱える人にはおすすめしない。これほどAIに失望させられたのははじめてだ。

ちなみに、特定の個人名を消し込んでいることについて、上記の内容を送ると、謝罪もせず以下のような言い訳をするゴミAI。
------------------------------------↓
GeminiはGoogleの安全ポリシーを考慮して設計されている。特定の業界、個人、企業に関する質問への回答を避ける場合がある。これには噂のようなセンシティブな話題や未確認情報も含まれる。目的は虚偽情報の拡散防止と、プライバシー

reviews.title: The AI overview ruined it
reviews.text: A few years ago, when you would Google something, the first result would be a passage from an article or otherwise trustworthy source, with the answer to your question highlighted. It was short, simple, and was written by an actual human. That feature has now been replaced with the AI overview, which is a million times less helpful. It gives lengthy and unnecessarily detailed explanations, which are sometimes just made up. This is especially frustrating when I’m trying to write down vocabulary for my school work. The AI overview tries so hard to sound smart and in the process makes simple concepts impossible to understand. The worst part is that you can’t even get rid of it. You can add “-ai” to the end of your search, but that sometimes can exclude actual trustable resources from the results (ESPECIALLY when researching an AI related topic). I haven’t found a single person who likes it and have had to change browsers on all of my devices. I beg of you Google, let me turn off the AI overview.
